reasons.min_ram_mb:
NPX-1245 / rule #59 (RAM + vCPU): EVE-NG timos.yml says 2048 MB / 1 vCPU; netplex keeps 4096 / 2.
Measured live THROUGH the platform on VM .83 (lab API + node start, console relay, timos-12.0.R6):
with EVE's 2048/1 (qemu argv -m 2097152k -smp 1) TiMOS reaches "Login:" only after ~1268 s; with
4096/2 it reaches it at ~636 s (Wave 21 U6). So EVE's value boots but is 2x slower and lands
past this profile's 750 s boot_timeout_sec. NOT tested: timos-21.10.R1 at 2048/1 (this key also
serves 21.x and that image could not be registered on the test VM this session) - so 4096 stays.
reasons.boot_timeout_sec:
Live-booted 2026-09-07 (Wave 21 U6 confirmation experiment, timos-12.0.R6):
given this profile's own 4096 MB/2 vCPU (now correctly matched thanks to
NPX-817's path-separator fix), a real TiMOS "Login: " prompt was reached at
t=636.2s (`repro_timos.log`) - past the previous 600s boot_timeout_sec,
which would still have flagged this genuine successful boot as a failure.
750s keeps real margin over the observed time.
